task_statement:
Research question (as posed on 2026-11-01, in the area of player absence and offensive reorganization):
How much the offense reorganizes (relative to L) predicts the change in points per possession.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): n=986; n=148, mde rho; 148 spells

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

research_concepts: offensive reorganization relative to baseline L
methodological_questions: How is offensive reorganization defined relative to baseline L, and is that definition reliable?
Does reorganization predict change in PPP at the spell level after accounting for confounders?
What minimum detectable effect does n=148 spells support, and is the study powered for it?
Do absences that trigger reorganization differ systematically from those that do not (selection)?

historical_evidence.finding: Study of whether real player absences move the association structure (V1) and whether a LOO simulation predicts the magnitude (V2). Record reports V1(a) 16/23 above own-null p95 (binomial p=2.67e-16) and V1(b) mean(D_real - median_null)=+0.142, CI [+0.103, +0.187], marked CONFIRMED; V2a Spearman +0.288, p=0.077, CI [-0.244, +0.667] FAIL; V2b partial +0.253, p=0.115 FAIL. Auto-limited by [prior work].

Comparison of V4 vs V5 player routing by observed PPP. Only 8 divergences, 0 scoreable (8 unscored because the player was missing from Neo4j); V5 mostly routed to 'team' rather than a player. Failure type recorded as A_unanswerable.

Routing prior vs H2H posterior gate. Reported mean PPP delta of +1.26 (n>=5) and +1.13 (n>=15) was judged small-sample inflation: low-n leaders are role players with 2-3 PPP on 5-7 possessions (e.g. n=6, PPP=3.00).

Live trigger timing (early vs late detection). Spearman tier vs BEST-counter outcomes reported as rho -0.2066, p=1e-06, n=557 in one version, while an earlier version reported rho=-0.0457, p=0.456, n=268 and a Mann-Whitney p=0.074 not confirmed at 0.05. Auto-confidence low (0.26). Only tangentially related to absence reorganization.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Testing whether the simulated absence-driven association magnitude matches the real association (V2a/V2b)
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as FAIL with wide CIs spanning zero (CI [-0.244, +0.667] and [-0.262, +0.615]); auto-limited by small sample. V1(b) was confirmed but V2 was not.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Comparing observed PPP of players routed by V4 vs V5 on divergent series
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as A_unanswerable: 0 of 8 divergences scoreable; player records missing from [source] database, so the question could not be answered with the data or design.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Using a PPP-lead gate at n>=5 or n>=15 to detect a routing signal
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as C_artifact: apparent effect was produced by small-sample inflation rather than real signal.

evidence_establishes: Earlier project work on closely related absence-validation questions (FAM:[prior work]) found small-sample limits: its association-magnitude tests were not significant and had CIs spanning zero.
Small per-unit samples in this project have produced artifactual PPP differences (FAM:[prior work]), so per-spell PPP outcomes need strong sample-size control.
Graph-database player coverage gaps have made earlier comparisons unscoreable ([prior work][prior work]), so data completeness must be verified before analysis.
evidence_does_not_establish: No retrieved record tests offensive reorganization relative to L against change in PPP, so the specific question has not been answered.
No retrieved record gives a reliability or validity estimate for a reorganization measure relative to L.
No record gives the minimum detectable effect for the 148-spell design; the input 'mde rho' has no stated value.
None of the retrieved records covers the 2025-26 partial data or the playoffs-versus-regular-season split for this question.
own_inferences: 'Relative to L' is not defined in the task statement or the data catalog, so the exposure cannot be specified or checked yet.
At alpha 0.05 and 80% power, n=148 detects a Spearman rho of roughly 0.23 (my own Fisher-z calculation). Smaller effects would be missed, and a null result would be uninformative.
Spells are likely clustered within players, teams and games, so effective sample size is below 148.
Measuring reorganization and PPP change from the same play-by-play window risks leakage and outcome-derived labels.
Absences that cause reorganization may be non-random (injury severity, minutes load), so the association may reflect selection rather than reorganization.
uncertainties: The meaning and computation of L and the reorganization metric are not given.
The actual MDE value and any pre-specified effect size are missing.
Whether the 148 spells are independent, and how many players and games they span, is unknown.
The 2025-26 playoffs are partial before 2026-06-21, and the 2025-26 regular season is complete only from 2026-04-13.
Full text of several records was truncated; read_family was not called, so some detail may be missing.

historical_effect.explanation: Earlier records showed that the closest analogous absence-validation test (FAM:[prior work]) was underpowered and untestable on its association magnitude, that small-sample PPP differences produced artifacts (FAM:[prior work]), and that player-level coverage gaps made comparisons unscoreable ([prior work][prior work]). These findings moved the decision from a direct test toward a hold until the exposure is defined, the MDE is computed, and data coverage is verified.

blocking_constraints.text: n=148 spells gives roughly 80% power only for rho about 0.23 or larger; no MDE value is stated, and the closest prior test was underpowered.
'Relative to L' is undefined, so the reorganization measure has no established reliability or validity.
Change in PPP is derived from the same play-by-play used to define reorganization, which risks a circular label.
Absences are not randomly assigned; injury severity and minutes load may drive both reorganization and PPP change.

prior_work.summary: No retrieved record tests offensive reorganization relative to L against change in PPP after player absence. FAM:[prior work] is the closest and studies absence structure and simulated magnitude, but its magnitude tests failed and were recorded as untestable with small samples. [prior work][prior work] and FAM:[prior work] concern routing and gating, and FAM:[prior work] concerns trigger timing; these are related only in method and data risk.

risks.text: Power for 148 spells is limited to large effects (rho about 0.23); the MDE must be computed before the run.
The reorganization measure relative to L lacks a defined, validated scale; test-retest and split-half reliability are unknown.
PPP change and reorganization share the play-by-play source, so their association may be partly mechanical.
If L or reorganization uses possessions after the absence, post-absence information leaks into the exposure.
Shot quality, usage, opponent, rest, minutes, team strength and game context may drive both reorganization and PPP change.
Absences with large reorganization may be those with more severe injuries or larger minutes loss, selecting the exposure non-randomly.
Some spells may have few possessions in the post-absence window, making PPP change noisy.
Pooling 2022-23 to 2025-26, regular season and playoffs, and partial 2025-26 data may mix different rotation and pace regimes.
Several reorganization metrics or windows tried against the same outcome would inflate false positives.
Null spells or shuffled absences may not be comparable, so placebo results may be unreliable.
Spells with reorganization above a threshold may be rare, which would limit effective sample size for the high-reorganization group.

design.estimand: Partial association (Spearman and a covariate-adjusted regression slope) between offensive reorganization relative to pre-absence baseline L and the change in PPP from pre-absence to post-absence windows, per absence spell. L and the reorganization metric must be defined in writing before data are touched.
design.unit: Absence spell (one player absence episode for one team), with the player and game clustering recorded.
design.sample: 148 spells from complete NBA 2022-23 to 2024-25 regular seasons and playoffs, plus 2025-26 regular season only after 2026-04-13. Exclude partial 2025-26 playoff data before 2026-06-21. Confirm spell count and player coverage in [source] database first.
design.power: Compute the MDE before running, using the effective sample size after clustering by player and game. At n=148 with no clustering, 80% power at alpha 0.05 detects rho about 0.23; a smaller effective n raises the threshold. Only proceed if the MDE is below a pre-specified substantive effect.
design.controls: Pre-absence PPP baseline, usage, minutes, shot quality/distance mix, opponent and team strength, rest, season and playoff indicator, absence cause or severity where available. Use only information before the absence for L and the exposure to avoid leakage.
design.falsification: Placebo: the same reorganization metric computed on matched non-absence windows should show no association with PPP change. Also check that the association is absent for pre-absence windows and that shuffled exposure gives null results.
design.multiplicity: One pre-specified primary metric and window. Secondary metrics and windows are exploratory and reported with correction (e.g. Holm). Report the number of metrics tried.
design.decision_rule: Primary: a pre-registered covariate-adjusted slope with a 95% CI; support only if the CI excludes zero and the placebo is null. Reject only if the CI excludes the pre-specified substantive effect and the MDE was met. Otherwise report as uncertain.
design.data_version: NBA stats API per-game files as of 2026-11-01, with complete seasons only; record the snapshot date and the 2025-26 completeness status for each file.
